extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, proprietors, agents/attorneys and patent office formalities officers (Singapore)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and formal requirements from the Singapore patent registry covering restoration of patents, re-examination after grant, extension of time, and inventorship matters. Used by applicants/proprietors/agents to prepare filings and by Formalities officers to assess compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration allowed where lapse was unintentional
rubrics_metrics.description: For patents lapsed on or after 14 Feb 2014, restoration is allowable if the proprietor can demonstrate that the lapse of the patent was unintentional; third parties’ rights which can accrue would be protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration may be requested within 18 months of the renewal due date. The 'unintentional' test is applied to the proprietor or any person entitled to the patent at the time renewal fees were payable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements for Restoration (Patents Form 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proprietor may request Restoration of Patent by filing Patents Form 19 together with a Statutory Declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of a sample Statutory Declaration is in the Appendix. Statutory Declaration or affidavit must be submitted within 14 days from date of receipt of Patents Form 19 (see formalities checklist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer checklist for Restoration applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request for restoration is received the Formalities officer will review: (a) fee has been paid; (b) the patent has lapsed; (c) the form is filed within 18 months after the renewal due date; (d) statutory declaration/affidavit submitted within 14 days from receipt of Patents Form 19; (e) applicant is proprietor or person entitled (joint proprietors: one or more may apply); (f) review the Statutory Declaration to determine whether the lapse is unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any requirement not met, the officer will invite clarification/rectification within 2 months; may request supplementary Statutory Declaration if reasons not satisfactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification and correction procedures for Restoration matters
rubrics_metrics.description: If defects are identified, applicants may be invited to clarify or rectify within 2 months; to rectify errors file Form CM4 indicating the relevant rule(s); to update representation/address file Form CM1 or CM2; submit clarifications/supplementary declarations/evidence via eCommunications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate CM4 option for form errors vs other documents. If unresolved, officer may refuse request; reminder(s) may be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement and effect of a restoration application
rubrics_metrics.description: If formal requirements are met, the Formalities officer will acknowledge and advertise the restoration application; advertisement entered in the register and published in the next Patents Journal; patent status updated to 'Lapsed (restoration pending)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advertisement constitutes the notice required by Section 39(4) and concludes the period under Section 39(10) protecting third parties who began in good faith to do acts that would have been infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment requirement after provisional allowance of restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Formalities officer is satisfied the application can be allowed, the proprietor will be notified to pay the additional fee for restoration and all unpaid renewal fee within 2 months from date of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not paid within 2 months, Registrar issues a reminder; applicant may still file Patents Form 20 together with request for extension of time (see extension rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Intention to Refuse and right to be heard (restoration)
rubrics_metrics.description: If officer is not satisfied lapse was unintentional, a Notice of Intention to Refuse will be issued. Within 1 month from date of notification, the proprietor may request to be heard by filing Form HC4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hearing outcome is refusal, applicant notified and application status remains unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Patents Form 20 to pay additional and unpaid renewal fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Proprietor may make payment of additional fee and renewal fee for Restoration by filing Patents Form 20 within 2 months from date of Registrar’s notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System reviews that Form 20 is filed within 2 months and the number of years of unpaid renewal fee is correctly indicated and paid. If requirements are met, system auto-issues letter confirming restoration and status updated to 'Patent in Force'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures when Patents Form 20 request is incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: If Patents Form 20 does not fulfil requirements for automatic completion, the Formalities officer will invite the applicant to clarify or rectify within 2 months; same correction channels (CM4, CM1/CM2, eCommunications) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unresolved or objections cannot be overcome, the request will be refused and status updated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-payment and extension possibilities for restoration fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If payment not received within 2 months of notification, Registrar issues a reminder; applicant may file Patents Form 20 with a request for extension of time. Multiple extensions up to 6 months from the original timeline may be requested via Patents Form 45 before end of 6 months. Extensions beyond 6 months possible if applicant satisfies Registrar of continuing underlying intention to proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may request multiple extensions; if not satisfied, system will refuse the restoration request and update register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examination after grant — who may request and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-examination after grant allows any person to request re-examination of a granted patent to revoke patents that should not have been granted and permits patentees to strengthen patents by amendment subject to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request may be filed any time after grant provided no other proceedings pending before the court or Registrar in which validity may be put in issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for re-examination after grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds include: (a) invention is not patentable; (b) specification does not disclose the invention clearly and completely for a person skilled in the art; (c) matter in specification extends beyond that disclosed in the application as filed; (d) amendment to patent specification results in disclosing additional matter or extends protection conferred; (e) amendment to application specification results in matter extending beyond that disclosed as filed; (f) a correction to the specification or application was wrongly allowed; (g) the patent is one of two or more patents for the same invention with same priority date filed by same party or successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grounds are generally limited to requirements considered during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements for re-examination (Patents Form 36)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for re-examination should be filed via Patents Form 36 selecting 'Request for re-examination after grant' together with the prescribed fee; the request should state reasons substantiating the ground and include any relevant documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee will be notified of the request. If documents are in another language, an English translation and VET may be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer checklist for re-examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Officer will review that: (a) fee has been paid; (b) the patent is granted; (c) statement identifying each ground and explaining how it is satisfied; (d) English translation and VET if needed; (e) patent is not pending before the court or Registrar in related proceedings; (f) request is not frivolous, vexatious or an abuse of process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements not met, officer invites clarification/rectification within 2 months; correction mechanisms (CM4, CM1/2, eCommunications) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome when re-examination request fulfils requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When request fulfils requirements and Registrar grants the request, it will be forwarded to the Patent Examiner to conduct re-examination and the applicant will be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Examiner will prepare and forward a re-examination report to the Registry on completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written opinion, interview rights and response timelines (re-examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Examiner finds a ground is made out, a Written Opinion is issued. The proprietor may request an interview with the Examiner within 2 months after Registrar sends the Written Opinion (Registrar must grant such a request). A response to the Written Opinion must be submitted with Patents Form 13A within 3 months from issuance; responses without the form or after 3 months will be disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses should contain written submissions or an application to amend the specification. Amendments must show deletions by striking through and replacements by underlining. If proprietor both submits submissions and applies for amendment, both must be done together. Failure to respond treats the Written Opinion as the re-examination report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner directions on amendments and effect on objections
rubrics_metrics.description: If Examiner considers a proposed amendment would resolve an objection, the Examiner must state so in the re-examination report and specify the objection resolved. The Registrar may direct the proprietor to file a specification incorporating the amendment within the time specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the re-examination report contains unresolved objections, the Registrar must order revocation or conditional revocation unless amended to satisfaction within a specified time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of revocation decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision of the Registrar to revoke a patent has effect from the date of the grant of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-examination request, written opinion and report are made available on the Patents Open Dossier. For more details refer to Examination Guidelines for Patent Applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time — general availability and Form 45
rubrics_metrics.description: A time period prescribed in the Rules or specified by the Registrar may be extended in some circumstances by filing Patents Form 45; extensions protect applicant rights and prevent abandonment where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions possible only for listed Rules. Some rules cannot be extended (Rule 108(2) list), some may be extended up to 6 months (Rule 108(3) list), some up to 18 months (Rule 108(4) list). Extensions must be requested before expiry and may be submitted in writing via eCommunications no later than 6 months after first expiry in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and filing requirements for EOT under Rule 108(3)/(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For EOT under Rule 108(3)/(4) (patent applications lodged on or after 14 Feb 2014): only one rule selected; form filed within 6 or 18 months depending on rule; total period of extension must not exceed 6 or 18 months; for pre-grant rules, patent should not be granted; application not withdrawn; representation/address for service must correspond with record (or CM1/CM2 filed and approved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If system criteria met, extension auto-approved and register updated. If status was 'Abandoned (EOT possible)' or 'Refused (EOT possible)' due to that time period, status updated to 'Pending (not published)' or 'Pending (published)' as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual review and rectification for EOT requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If EOT request does not satisfy automatic approval criteria, the Formalities officer will manually review requirements and may invite clarification/rectification within 2 months. Applicants may use CM4, CM1/CM2 and eCommunications to rectify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If objections cannot be overcome or no response, the officer will refuse the request and the application status remains unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: EOT as of right under Rule 108(5) — specific criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For EOT as of right under Rule 108(5) (Patents Form 45 for applications lodged on or after 14 Feb 2014): fee paid; for pre-grant rules, patent not granted; representation/address match record; extension as of right exhausted for apps before 14 Feb 2014; form filed within 6 or 18 months for post-14 Feb apps; Statutory Declaration/affidavit filed demonstrating continuing underlying intention (CUI) to proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements unmet officer invites clarification; may request supplementary Statutory Declaration. If objections cannot be overcome, officer issues Notification of Intention to Refuse; applicant may request hearing via Form HC4 within 1 month. If extension refused for apps on/after 14 Feb 2014, refund made for additional fees paid for the extension period sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and protection for persons affected by Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrar will publish notification in the Patents Journal where he has granted a total extension of more than 6 months under Rule 108(1) or an extension under Rule 108(5); similar publication for court decisions varying Registrar decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person who availed himself or took definite steps to avail himself of the invention due to the act not being done within time (because extension granted) has right to continue to avail himself of the invention (but cannot grant a licence to another). If done in course of business, rights may be authorised to partners or assigned/transmitted on death/dissolution. Disposal of a product by such a person treated as if disposed by the proprietor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to be mentioned as inventor and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor(s) have a right to be mentioned in any patent and published application for the invention unless another person is entitled by law, treaty, convention or agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may identify inventors in Patents Form 1 (Applicant & Inventor Details) parts 3.3/3.4 or file Patents Form 8 to identify inventors and derivation of rights. For PCT national phase entry, a separate Form 8 is not required if inventorship already declared in PCT application (duplicate records can be removed upon request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for filing Patents Form 8 (mention of inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents Form 8 must be filed within specified timelines: (a) Normal application: 16 months from declared priority date or from filing date if no priority; (b) Divisional: 16 months from declared priority or filing date, or on initiation date of divisional (whichever later); (c) PCT national phase: 16 months from priority or filing date or 2 months from national phase start (whichever later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National phase entry begins when early national phase entry requested and requirements satisfied, or at expiry of 30 months or extended time period for normal/late entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer checklist for inventor mention filings
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of Patents Form 8 the Formalities officer will review: (a) form filed within timelines or extension approved; (b) at least one inventor named; (c) derivation of rights indicated (Part 6); (d) representation/address for service correspond with that on record (or CM1/CM2 filed and approved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements not met, officer will invite clarification/rectification within 2 months; corrections via CM4, CM1/CM2, or eCommunications apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to file Form 8 or remedying defects
rubrics_metrics.description: If objections cannot be overcome or there is no response, the request will be refused and applicant notified. If time for filing Patents Form 8 has passed, the application will be treated as abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all requirements are met, officer will approve and notify applicant(s)/inventor(s) and make register and Patents Journal entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition and removal of inventors (Patents Form 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person alleging he ought to have been mentioned as inventor may file Patents Form 7 to add himself; a person alleging that someone ought not to have been mentioned may file Patents Form 7 to remove the inventor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single Patents Form 7 may be used if the same person seeks both to add himself and remove the inventor(s) mentioned. Patents Form 7 must be filed together with a statement setting out fully the facts relied upon for the addition and/or removal of inventor(s).
